text: “You took your time,” {he} said. “I’ve been here long enough to be charged rent.”
“Not so loud,” {he} said, although I hadn’t said anything yet. “Sit down and look like you’re here for the drinks.”
“Well?” {he} said. “Sit down. The police already stood around, and look where that got anybody.”
“There you are,” {he} said. “I was starting to think I’d hired the other kind of detective. The kind that sleeps.”
“Keep your voice down,” {he} said. “Half this room thinks I did it, and the other half hasn’t heard yet.”
“Sit with me,” {he} said. “If they’re going to stare, they can stare at two of us.”
“Anything?” {he} said. “Don’t answer that. Sit down first, then tell me nothing.”
“You look like a man who’s been looking,” {he} said. “Sit down and look somewhere else for a minute.”
“You came,” {he} said, as if that had been in some doubt. “Good. I’ve been watching the door all night.”
“I didn’t think you’d find this place,” {he} said. “That’s a compliment to the place, not to you.”
“{victim} still owes me,” {he} said, by way of hello. “Sit down. I’d like somebody at this table on my side of that.”
{He} moved {his} coat off the other chair, which was as much hello as I was going to get.
“There you are,” {he} said. “Sit. You’re making the room nervous, standing.”
“You found it,” {he} said. “I was hoping you would, and a little hoping you wouldn’t.”
“Sit,” {he} said, barely moving {his} lips. “And keep your voice where I keep mine.”
“Don’t wave,” {he} said. “People in here remember a man who waves.”
{He} didn’t get up. “Everybody else has given up on it,” {he} said. “Sit down and don’t.”
“Sit down,” {he} said. “You’re on my money now, so you may as well be comfortable.”
“Before you say anything, I know how it looks,” {he} said. “I’ve been sitting here looking at how it looks, and it looks worse every time somebody new comes in.”
“Let them look,” {he} said, without looking at anybody. “Sit where they can see you too.”
“Sit down,” {he} said. “I’d rather not talk about it standing up, and I’d rather not talk about it at all.”
{He} nodded at the chair and not at me. “You know what I want back,” {he} said. “Don’t say it in here.”
“I’ve told myself it will turn up about forty times since I sat down,” {he} said. “You’re the first one who might make it true.”
“Quick, sit, before the whole room decides you’re a policeman,” {he} said. “You have the walk. They all have the walk.”
“Not here,” {he} said, and then, when I didn’t move, “Well. Sit, then.”
“You’re quicker than the police,” {he} said. “Keep it that way, and sit down.”
“Have you heard anything? Has anybody said anything? You’d tell me,” {he} said, all in one breath. “Sit. No, there, where I can see the door.”
{He} looked past me at the door, and then at me. “Not yet, then,” {he} said.
“Every time that door opens I think it’s {victim},” {he} said. “Then it’s somebody like you. Sit down.”
“I don’t want to talk about it here, and I don’t want to talk about it anywhere else either,” {he} said. “Sit down. You make me nervous, hovering.”
“Sit,” {he} said. “And don’t say the name. I’ve got used to not hearing it.”
“You’re late, which is good,” {he} said. “Nobody watches the door this late.”
“{victim} owed me, you know, and I don’t mind who hears it,” {he} said. “Well, I mind a little. Sit down.”
“Money,” {he} said, as if that was hello. “Sit down.”
“I’m out a good deal already,” {he} said. “Sit down before it’s more.”
“There you are. I was about to send out for you or for another drink, whichever came first,” {he} said. “Sit, sit.”
“You found it! Most people walk straight past,” {he} said. “I walked straight past it twice, and I knew where it was.”
“Sit,” {he} said. It was all {he} said for a while.
“You,” {he} said, as if that settled something. “Good.”
“Sit down before somebody takes that chair,” {he} said. “It’s the only one in here that doesn’t wobble.”
“Anything?” {he} said, before I was all the way in. “No. Of course not. Sit down, you’ve been walking.”
“I keep thinking I hear it scratching at the door,” {he} said. “Then it’s only the door. Sit down, sit down.”
“Sit down,” {he} said. “I’ve looked under this table twice already, in case you were wondering.”
{He} moved a glass so I could sit. “It’s still missing,” {he} said, and looked at my hands in case I’d brought it.
“Keep your voice down,” {he} said. “Sit. If {victim} walks in, we’re talking about the weather.”
“{victim} asked me tonight if I’d seen it, and I said no, which is true, more or less,” {he} said. “Sit down. Tell me something good.”
“Well?” {he} said. “Sit down. Tell me slowly, or don’t tell me at all.”
{He} didn’t look up. “Sit,” {he} said. “Whatever it is, I’d rather hear it sitting down.”
“You’re smiling,” {he} said. “Are you smiling? Sit down and tell me why.”
“I told myself I wouldn’t ask the minute you walked in,” {he} said. “Well? Sit down. I’m asking.”
